What do you want right now, honestly?

strong.text: Your chart is the strong kind, {dm_short}, so add one more layer to the story above. Strong charts remember a relationship as a series of positions they held. You can probably recite your case: what you asked for, what they failed to do, the night it became obvious. Most of it may even be accurate. What a strong chart files away is how much room was left for the other person to be right about anything. Try this once, on paper. Write the three complaints they would make about you, in their words, at their most reasonable. Not the cruel version, the fair one. If you can't think of three, that's the finding. If you can, you now hold the half of the story you were missing, and you can stop arguing with someone who isn't in the room.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Write their three fair complaints about you. Their version, not your rebuttal.

weak.text: Your chart is the weak kind, {dm_short}, which shapes how you tell this story. A weak chart tends to take the whole bill. You may have already decided it ended because you were too much, or not enough, or both at once, depending on the hour. That feels like honesty. It is closer to habit. Try sorting it into three piles: what was yours, what was theirs, and what belonged to the timing, the city, the job, the season of life you were both in. Most breakups split across all three. If your first pile is enormous and the other two are empty, you are not being accurate, you are being polite to someone who is gone. Give the other piles their fair share. It doesn't excuse anything you did. It just puts the weight where it actually sits.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Three piles: yours, theirs, and the timing. You don't get to carry all of them.

rat.text: Saju reads the branch sitting under your Day Master as the spouse palace, the private room a partner lives in. Yours holds the Rat, 子, deep winter Water and one of the four peach-blossom branches tied to charm. Up close you are clever, nocturnal, emotionally deeper than you let on, and careful about who gets the real version. After a breakup the Rat goes underground: lots of thinking, very little showing. The useful question for you is whether your ex ever met the burrow, or only the bright, witty surface. If they didn't, part of what ended was a relationship with half of you in it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rat spouse palace. Did they ever meet the real you, or just the clever one?

ox.text: Saju reads the branch sitting under your Day Master as the spouse palace, the private room a partner lives in. Yours holds the Ox, 丑, cold wet Earth that stores Metal and Water. In love the Ox is loyal, patient and slow to let go, which is exactly why breakups take you longer than your friends expect. You don't switch off. You carry the field until you're sure it's fallow. That loyalty is a virtue. It also means you may still be keeping promises to a relationship that has released you from them. Write down one promise you're still keeping, and decide whether you want to.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ox spouse palace: still keeping old promises. You're allowed to set them down.

tiger.text: Saju reads the branch sitting under your Day Master as the spouse palace, the private room a partner lives in. Yours holds the Tiger, 寅, early-spring Wood with Fire inside, and one of the travel branches readers call yeokma. Up close you need movement, honesty and a partner who doesn't try to tame you. When things end, the Tiger's reflex is to leap somewhere new, a city, a job, a person. Sometimes that's healthy. Sometimes it's running with style. Before your next big leap, sit still long enough to name what you're leaping away from.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Tiger spouse palace: you leap away from pain. Sit for a minute first.

rabbit.text: Saju reads the branch sitting under your Day Master as the spouse palace, the private room a partner lives in. Yours holds the Rabbit, 卯, pure spring Wood and one of the peach-blossom branches. Up close you're gentle, aesthetic and conflict-shy. You probably kept the peace in this relationship, and it may have ended partly because the real disagreements were never spoken. That isn't a character flaw. It is a habit that can change. In the next relationship, say the small disagreement while it's still small. Peace that is kept by silence tends to end suddenly.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rabbit spouse palace: you kept the peace. Next time, keep the truth too.

dragon.text: Saju reads the branch sitting under your Day Master as the spouse palace, the private room a partner lives in. Yours holds the Dragon, 辰, damp spring Earth that stores Water. Storehouse branches keep things, and the Dragon keeps big hopes and private plans. You may have imagined a whole future with this person, one they never fully saw. That's why the loss can feel larger to you than the relationship looked from outside. You're grieving the stored future too. Name it, on paper. Then decide which parts of that future you could still build without them.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dragon spouse palace: you're grieving a future they never saw. Name it.

snake.text: Saju reads the branch sitting under your Day Master as the spouse palace, the private room a partner lives in. Yours holds the Snake, 巳, early-summer Fire with Metal hidden in it, and one of the travel branches. Up close you're observant, private and slow to trust, and once hurt, you can go very cold. After this breakup you may have shed the relationship like a skin, neatly and silently. Check underneath. Snakes are good at looking finished. Let one trusted person see the part that isn't.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Snake spouse palace: you look finished with it. Let one person see the rest.

horse.text: Saju reads the branch sitting under your Day Master as the spouse palace, the private room a partner lives in. Yours holds the Horse, 午, midsummer Fire and one of the peach-blossom branches. Up close you're passionate, honest and allergic to feeling penned in. Breakups hit you fast and loud, and you move fast and loud afterward too. That speed protects you and also skips steps. Before you gallop into the next thing, walk a lap. What did this relationship give you that you'd want again? What did it cost that you won't pay twice?

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Horse spouse palace: walk one lap before the next gallop.

goat.text: Saju reads the branch sitting under your Day Master as the spouse palace, the private room a partner lives in. Yours holds the Goat, 未, warm late-summer Earth that stores Wood. Up close you're tender, artistic and a quiet worrier, the one who looked after the mood of the relationship. After a breakup the Goat worries about the other person's feelings almost as much as its own. That's kind, and it can delay your own grief. Give your worry a new address for a while: you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Goat spouse palace: you're worrying about their feelings. Worry about yours.

monkey.text: Saju reads the branch sitting under your Day Master as the spouse palace, the private room a partner lives in. Yours holds the Monkey, 申, early-autumn Metal with Water inside, and one of the travel branches. Up close you're quick, funny and restless, and you probably got through the worst days of this breakup with jokes. Humor is a real strength. It is also a door you close on the feeling. Let one conversation about the breakup stay unfunny from start to finish. You'll be surprised how much lighter you feel afterward.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Monkey spouse palace: great breakup jokes. Now have one unfunny conversation.

rooster.text: Saju reads the branch sitting under your Day Master as the spouse palace, the private room a partner lives in. Yours holds the Rooster, 酉, pure autumn Metal and one of the peach-blossom branches. Up close you're precise, honest and exacting, and you have a sharp eye for what went wrong. After a breakup the Rooster can turn that eye on itself and pick every flaw. Use the precision kindly. Name one thing you'd do differently, specifically, and one thing you did well, just as specifically. Both lists deserve the same attention to detail.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rooster spouse palace: list what you did well, with the same precision.

dog.text: Saju reads the branch sitting under your Day Master as the spouse palace, the private room a partner lives in. Yours holds the Dog, 戌, dry autumn Earth that stores Fire. Up close you're loyal and protective, slow to trust and fierce once you do. That's why betrayal, or anything that felt like it, cuts so deep. You may still be standing guard over the relationship, defending it to friends or defending yourself against it. You can stop patrolling. Loyalty is meant for people who are here, starting with you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dog spouse palace: you're still guarding a house nobody lives in. Come home.

pig.text: Saju reads the branch sitting under your Day Master as the spouse palace, the private room a partner lives in. Yours holds the Pig, 亥, early-winter Water with Wood inside, and one of the travel branches. Up close you're warm, trusting and generous, quick to forgive and quick to hope. After a breakup that generosity can keep you rewriting the story so your ex comes out well. Kind, but not always accurate. Let the story include the times you were let down too. Seeing them clearly doesn't make you less kind.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Pig spouse palace: you keep forgiving the story. Let it be accurate too.

base.why-it-ended: Gap Wood grows straight up, and that's both the gift and the problem. In your last relationship you probably knew where you were going, and you assumed they were coming with you. When things got hard, you didn't bend. You explained, you planned, you fixed. What you may not have done is ask what they needed and then actually wait for the answer. A breakup with a tall tree is rarely about one fight. It's about a slow feeling, on their side or yours, of living inside someone else's plan. That isn't a crime. It's a habit, and habits can be seen. Name it honestly and you already hold more of this story than you think.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You loved hard and planned a whole future. That's not a flaw, Gap.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Sure. You just forgot to ask if they wanted the same future.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Missing them doesn't mean leaving was wrong.

spring.intro: Born in spring, Gap Wood, you arrived when every tree was shooting upward at once. Wood was in command of the season, so your chart got a double dose of yourself: tall, certain, rooted. In a breakup that means you probably decided early what the story was and have defended it ever since. You were right about some of it. The spring tree's problem is that it grows toward the light without checking what it shaded on the way. If they said you never bent, they may have had a point. The good news comes from the same place: a spring tree regrows fast. Your recovery starts properly once you stop arguing the case in your head.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You won that argument in your head four hundred times. Feel better yet?

summer.intro: Summer-born Gap Wood grows in heat. Fire ruled your birth month, and a tree's whole job in summer is to feed that fire, so your chart pours energy outward: plans, effort, big gestures, words. In love you probably gave a lot and said a lot. Maybe too much of both in the final months, when the gestures got louder because the connection felt quieter. A summer tree can scorch itself and call it devotion. The breakup may have left you less heartbroken than burnt out, and those two feel identical at 2am. Rest is your relief: quiet, people who ask nothing of you. Let yourself be watered before you decide what any of it meant.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You gave so much it singed you a little. Rest first, decide later.

autumn.intro: Autumn is the axe season for a tree. Metal held the season you were born in, Gap Wood, and Metal cuts Wood. That's why you carry a stern inner judge. You hold yourself to rules, and after a breakup you likely turned that blade inward: a list of every mistake, reviewed nightly. Autumn trees also learn to drop their leaves and survive, which is the gift buried in this chart. You can let something go cleanly once you've truly decided it's done. The danger is deciding too fast, out of pride, and then quietly checking their profile for months to make sure you were right. Pruning is meant to help growth. Make sure you're pruning, not punishing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your inner judge has held court every night this month. Adjourn, please.

winter.intro: A winter tree looks bare, but its roots are drinking. Water rules winter, and Water feeds Wood, so your season feeds you underneath even when it looks still on top. In a breakup you probably went quiet. Fewer posts, fewer words, a lot of thinking. People may assume you're fine, or cold. You're neither. You're absorbing. The risk for winter Wood is that all that nourishment turns into overthinking: you keep feeding the memory instead of the next season. Rereading old messages counts as watering the past. You have more in reserve than you feel right now. The spring in you is real. It just needs warmth, daylight and other people to start moving.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You look still, Gap. Underneath, your roots are busy healing you.

earth.intro: You were born in the Earth days, the last stretch of a season, when the old weather fades and the ground takes over. For a Gap Wood that means a tree standing in heavy soil. Wood controls Earth, so you spent the relationship holding ground: plans, logistics, the shared calendar, the version of the future you kept steering toward. After the breakup the pull back is unfinished business. You built something, and leaving it half done feels wrong. The soil was never yours to carry alone. Write down what you built for yourself, not for the two of you, and start there.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're not missing them, Gap. You're missing the project. Different grief.

cliff.text: Here's how you tend to end things: late. Gap Wood stays because leaving feels like failing, and you don't fail, you persevere.

sample.text: Gap Wood wants to be understood, and a breakup leaves the case open.

base.why-it-ended: Eul Wood is the vine, the flower, the plant that finds light through a crack in the pavement. You adapt beautifully. In your last relationship you probably adapted a little too well. You bent around their schedule, their moods, their friends, until the shape of you got hard to find. Maybe they lost interest in someone who always agreed. Maybe you got tired of being flexible and never chosen. Either way, the ending likely came after a long quiet stretch of you saying it's fine when it wasn't. That's the part worth looking at. Not to blame yourself, but to remember that your needs were in the room too.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You gave so much, Eul. Being soft isn't why it ended.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: No, but saying it's fine forty times probably didn't help.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Missing them is just your heart looking for warmth.

spring.intro: Spring-born Eul Wood came up in the greenest month of the year, surrounded by other growing things. Wood was in charge, which gave your vine plenty of support and plenty of competition. In love that shows up as attachment that wraps fast and wraps well. You knew their friends, their coffee order, their mom's birthday. When it ended, you didn't lose one person, you lost a whole trellis. That's why it feels so structural. Spring vines also re-root easily, which can be a blessing or a trap: the easiest wall to climb is the one you already know. Before you reach back toward the old trellis, ask which you're missing: the person, or the support.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You don't miss them. You miss the wall you were climbing. Different problem.

summer.intro: Summer Eul Wood is a flower in full bloom, which looks gorgeous and costs a lot. Fire commanded your birth season and Wood feeds Fire, so your energy naturally flows out as charm, warmth and visible effort. In the relationship you likely made everything look effortless while working hard behind the scenes. Then the breakup, and suddenly nobody's watching the bloom. Summer flowers wilt when they're over-exposed: too many updates, too many friends asking, too much replaying out loud. You might be performing okay-ness on your stories while privately checking theirs. Shade is not hiding. Give yourself a few quiet weeks where you're not blooming for anyone, especially an audience of one.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Posting a glowing selfie for one specific viewer is not healing, Eul.

autumn.intro: Autumn hits a flower harder than a tree. Metal ruled when you were born, Eul Wood, and Metal is the element that controls and cuts Wood. You grew up under a season of pressure, which made you adaptable and very good at reading what others expect. In love you likely bent around them: their schedule, their moods, their version of events. The breakup might have felt like the shears finally closing. Here's the autumn secret: vines survive cutting better than almost anything. You will grow back. What matters is where. Not toward someone who made you smaller to fit. Toward a support that holds you without pruning you every week.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Vines grow back stronger after cutting. You're already sending out new shoots.

winter.intro: Winter Eul Wood is the bulb under frozen ground: quiet, patient, holding the whole flower inside. Water rules winter and nourishes Wood, so you have deep emotional reserves, but cold water also keeps you still. After the breakup you probably retreated inward, replaying conversations with the attention of a novelist. You feel everything and show almost nothing. That can make an ex think you didn't care, when really you cared in a season where nothing shows above ground. The pull for you is memory. You revisit it because it's warm in there. Bring a little warmth into your days: sunlight, a loud friend, a plan with a date on it. Bulbs need warmth to remember they're flowers.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You cared more than you showed. That's winter, not coldness.

earth.intro: Late in a season the ground hardens and Earth takes command. You arrived in those Earth days, Eul, a vine on packed soil, finding a way to grow anyway. Wood controls Earth, so in love you probably worked around every obstacle: the plans that kept moving, the moods you learned to predict, the people who never quite warmed up. You adapted so smoothly that nobody saw the effort. Now the pull back is the routine you wove around them. Your days still bend toward a shape that isn't there. Bend toward something of yours. A class, a new walk, a Sunday ritual that belongs to you alone.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You grew around every wall for them, Eul. Grow toward something just for you now.

cliff.text: Your breakups are rarely clean. Eul Wood doesn't cut, it untangles, one tendril at a time.

sample.text: For you, the pull is connection itself.

base.why-it-ended: Byeong Fire is the sun. You shine on everyone, generously and loudly, and that's your magic. In a relationship, though, the sun can be a lot. You may have filled every room, every plan, every silence, and your partner might have loved your energy while still feeling slightly invisible next to it. Or it went the other way: you gave warmth and got a cooler climate back, until you burned out and stopped trying. Sun types often end things with a big honest explosion or a sudden total loss of interest. Either way, it rarely came from nowhere. Look at the months before. The clues were in the weather.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Your warmth was real, Byeong. They felt it.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: They also felt there was no room left in the spotlight.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: It's okay to grieve loudly. That's honest.

spring.intro: A spring sun rises into a world that's growing just for it. Wood ruled your birth season and Wood feeds Fire, so you were born well fueled, Byeong: optimistic, generous, sure that warmth fixes things. In the relationship you probably believed love would win if you just shone harder. When it ended, the shock was less about them and more about a rule breaking. You gave light and it wasn't enough. That's hard for a spring sun to accept. The pull back often comes from there rather than from missing the person. You want to prove the rule still works. It does. Just not on everyone, and never as a way to earn someone staying.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Shining harder was never going to fix it. Some people just prefer shade.

summer.intro: Born in summer, you're the sun at noon, Byeong. Fire ruled the season and doubled your own element, so your chart runs hot: big feelings, big presence, big exits. Breakups for summer suns tend to be dramatic and then strangely fast. Either you blazed through the hurt in a week of loud nights out, or you burned so bright in the fights that there was nothing left to say. The blind spot is heat. Too much of it and nothing near you can grow, including a relationship. If you keep checking their stories, notice whether you're looking for them or for proof they still feel your warmth. Let noon cool to afternoon. That's where you see clearly.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Three nights out in a row is not closure. It's a heatwave.

autumn.intro: An autumn sun sits lower and more golden, Byeong, and it works harder for every degree of warmth. Metal held the season you were born in, and Fire's job is to melt and shape Metal. That gives your chart a practical streak: you show love through effort, plans, fixing things. In the relationship you may have treated it like a project you could forge into shape. When it broke, you probably asked what you did wrong, as if the right technique would have saved it. Some things don't melt. That's not a skill failure. The autumn sun's real strength is honesty: low light shows every detail. Use it on the relationship as it was, not the version you were building.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You worked so hard on it. That effort says lovely things about you.

winter.intro: A winter sun is precious because it's rare. Water ruled your birth season, Byeong, and Water is the element that puts out Fire. You grew up shining against the cold, which made you brave and a little defensive about your warmth. In love you may have expected the chill to arrive eventually, and braced for it. After the breakup you likely went bright on the outside and freezing underneath. Lots of laughing, little sleeping. Here's the winter truth: you're not too much. You were born into a season that tested your light, and you kept it anyway. The pull back is the worry that nobody else will feel that warm. Plenty of people already do.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You kept your light through a whole winter. That doesn't go out now.

earth.intro: The Earth days close each season, and you were born in them, Byeong. Fire feeds Earth, so your warmth went into the ground: into the relationship, the home, the friends you made feel welcome. The sun shining on a field gets very little back except a harvest someone else collects. After it ended you may feel strangely empty rather than heartbroken. That emptiness is what's left after giving. The pull back is the urge to warm someone, anyone, again. Before you shine on the next person, sit in the light yourself for a while. Rest counts.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're not cold, Byeong. You're out of fuel. Refill before you text.

cliff.text: You grieve out loud. Byeong Fire tells friends, posts the sad song, cries in the car, then goes out dancing three days later.

sample.text: What pulls you back is the memory of the best days, the big ones.

base.why-it-ended: Jeong Fire is the candle: intimate, focused, the light people sit close to. You love with intensity and pay attention to tiny things, a shift in tone, a reply that came later than usual. That sensitivity makes you a deep partner. It also means you probably noticed the ending long before anyone said it, and maybe you started grieving while you were still in it. Candle types read meaning into small silences and then protect themselves by pulling back first. If this breakup felt like a slow flicker rather than a crash, that's why. Ask yourself honestly: what did I feel early, and did I ever say it out loud?

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You noticed everything, Jeong. That's how deeply you loved.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: You also saw the ending months early and said nothing. Classic.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Your 2am feelings are real, but they're not the whole truth.

spring.intro: A candle lit in spring has wood stacked all around it. Wood commanded your birth season, Jeong, and Wood feeds Fire, so your inner flame is well supplied with feeling, memory and care. You love with focus: one person, fully seen. That's why this breakup hurts in such detail. You remember the song in the car, the exact wording of that text, the way they said your name. Your fuel is memory itself, and right now you're burning it to keep warm. It works until it doesn't. The spring candle's gift is renewal. You can light from fresh wood: new friends, new rooms, new stories. You don't have to keep burning the old ones.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're using old texts as firewood. That supply runs out, Jeong.

summer.intro: A candle in midsummer is a candle in a room full of other flames. Fire held the season you were born in, Jeong, so your chart carries a lot of your own element, which makes you intense, loyal and quietly fierce. In love you probably gave everything to a small circle of two. When it ended, the heat had nowhere to go. You might be burning it as anger, or as hours of analysis, or as a playlist you can't stop replaying. Summer Jeong can mistake intensity for meaning: it hurts this much, so it must be the one. Not necessarily. Sometimes it hurts this much because you're built to burn steadily. Let the flame settle before you read anything into it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: It hurting this much doesn't make them the one. You just burn hot.

autumn.intro: Autumn Jeong is the candle in the jeweler's workshop, the precise flame that shapes metal. Metal was in command when you were born, and Fire works on Metal, so your love is attentive and crafted. You noticed details, got things just right, remembered something they mentioned once in March. In the relationship you might have spent your flame refining someone who didn't want reshaping, or refining yourself to fit them. The breakup leaves you holding all that careful work. It wasn't wasted. It's a skill, and it belongs to you. The pull back is wanting the craft to have counted. It did. It doesn't need their approval to be real.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: All that care you crafted? Still yours. It goes wherever you go.

winter.intro: A candle in winter matters more than any other light. Water ruled your birth season, Jeong, and Water puts out Fire, so you grew up protecting your flame from drafts. That's why you trust slowly and love deeply once you do. In the relationship you probably cupped your hands around them. After the breakup, the draft got in. You may feel unusually small and flickery right now, and you might be checking their accounts as if hunting for the window that let the cold in. You won't find a full answer there. Winter candles survive inside a lantern: steady people, routines, warm places. Build yours before you go looking for anyone's draft.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Feeling flickery is allowed. Let your people be the lantern for a while.

earth.intro: You came in during the Earth days, Jeong, the weeks when a season winds down and soil takes over. A candle in a clay room: your flame warms the walls, and the walls keep the heat. Fire feeds Earth, so in love you poured attention into making things feel safe and settled. After the breakup, you might replay whether you gave enough. You did. Probably more than enough. The pull back is the comfort you built, not necessarily the person. Keep the comfort. Light it for yourself: your room, your music, your evenings.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: The warm room was your work, Jeong. You get to keep it.

cliff.text: You hold a breakup close. Jeong Fire doesn't announce, it processes, privately and thoroughly, usually around two in the morning.

sample.text: You let very few people into the small, warm room where your real self lives, and they were in there.

base.why-it-ended: Mu Earth is the mountain: steady, protective, impossible to push around. You were probably the solid one in that relationship, the person who showed up and held everything together. Mountains are wonderful to lean on. They're also hard to move. If your partner wanted change, spontaneity or more open emotion, they may have felt like they were knocking on rock. Or you carried too much for too long without ever saying how heavy it was, until the ground cracked. Either way, look at the moments you chose stillness when something in you already knew a conversation was needed.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You held everything together, Mu. That took real strength.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: It also took zero sentences about how you felt. Rocks can talk.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Missing your old routine is normal. It was home.

spring.intro: Spring is when roots break open the mountain. Wood ruled your birth season, Mu, and Wood controls Earth, so you were born under steady pressure to hold firm while things grew all over you. That made you dependable and very patient. Back then you held still, absorbing their changes and moods without moving. When it ended, you might be confused because you didn't do anything wrong, and that's partly the point. Spring mountains forget they're allowed to move. Some of what pushed through you was growth, some was damage, and you let both in quietly. The honest question isn't whether they come back. It's what you'd stop absorbing if they did.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You absorbed everything and called it being steady. Mountains get cracks too.

summer.intro: A summer mountain is warm right through. Fire ruled your season, Mu, and Fire generates Earth, so your chart is well supported: confident, generous, hard to knock over. That's a real gift in a breakup. You will be okay, probably faster than you expect. The blind spot of sunlit Earth is certainty. You knew what the relationship was, you knew what you were offering, and it may have been hard for them to change anything about it. Mountains don't negotiate. If you're replaying the end, look for the moments they asked you to move and you stayed put out of habit. That's not blame. It's the part you can actually work with.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: They asked you to budge. You were a mountain about it. Literally.

autumn.intro: An autumn mountain gives up its ore. Metal ruled your season, Mu, and Earth generates Metal, so your energy pours out as results: practical help, steady action, things done. In love you probably showed up with deeds more than words. The breakup may have left you puzzled. You did so much, so why wasn't it enough? Sometimes the other person wanted the words, the feelings, the slow talk that deeds can't replace. Autumn Earth also tires quietly, because it gives without noticing it's being mined. If you feel hollow rather than heartbroken, that's why. Refill before you decide anything. Fire helps: warmth, rest, people who look after you for once.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You did so much for them, Mu. Let someone do something for you.

winter.intro: A winter mountain holds back a frozen river. Your birth season belonged to Water, Mu, and Earth controls Water, so you were born to be the dam: steady, containing, keeping big feelings in their banks. In the relationship you probably managed a lot, maybe their emotions as well as yours. After the breakup, the dam held. You look calm. Inside there's more water pressing than anyone knows. The pull back for winter Mu is responsibility: wondering whether they're okay, whether you should check in, whether you held it together well enough. Let some of the river through. Cry, talk, write it out. A dam that never releases isn't strong. It's just very full.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Checking if they're okay is still checking. Ask if you're okay.

earth.intro: Born in the Earth days, Mu, you are a mountain in its own season, and that doubles everything solid about you. You stayed steady through the whole relationship, maybe steadier than they could match. When it ended you didn't crumble. You just went very still. The pull back for you is loyalty: the feeling that a commitment is a commitment, even after it's over. That isn't weakness. It's how mountains work. But stillness can turn into waiting. Notice if you're keeping a door open out of principle rather than wanting.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Being loyal to a finished thing isn't loyalty, Mu. It's parking.

cliff.text: You don't break, you erode. Mu Earth endures a lot quietly and gives a relationship every possible chance.

sample.text: The thing that pulls you back is loyalty and habit.

base.why-it-ended: Gi Earth is the garden: soft soil, generous, the place where things grow. You probably nurtured that relationship like something you loved tending. You remembered their appointments, handled the logistics, smoothed out their stress. Gardens give without asking, which is beautiful, and it can quietly turn you into the caretaker instead of the partner. Maybe they got comfortable and stopped tending you back. Maybe you got so busy keeping things alive that you forgot to check whether you still wanted to be there. Either way, the ending probably followed a long season of you giving more than you received.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You looked after them so well, Gi. That was love.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: It was also unpaid management. Did they ever water you back?

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: It wasn't all your fault. Two people built that garden.

spring.intro: Spring soil gets dug up, planted in and asked to feed everything. Your birth season belonged to Wood, Gi, and Wood controls Earth, so you grew up making room for other people's growth. In love that means you nurtured: their plans, their confidence, their moods. You were the field they grew in. After a breakup, soil like yours often feels depleted and strangely guilty, as if a failed harvest were your fault. It wasn't. Some seeds don't take, however good the ground. The pull back may be the urge to keep tending something already gone. Give yourself a fallow season. Fields that rest grow better crops, and the next one should be yours.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Good soil doesn't owe anyone a harvest. Rest, Gi. You've earned it.

summer.intro: Summer soil is warm, rich and ready. Your season belonged to Fire, Gi, and Fire feeds Earth, so your chart is nourished and steady at its core. You love practically and generously, and you probably held the relationship together in a hundred small ways nobody counted. The risk for well-fed Gi is that you also absorb a lot: their stress, their silences, their version of the breakup. You might still be carrying feelings that were never yours. Before asking whether they'll return, sort through what you're holding. Which feelings belong to you, and which came with them? Soil can be generous and still have edges. Your warm season means you recover well once you put down what isn't yours.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Half the sadness you're carrying is theirs. Return to sender, Gi.

autumn.intro: Autumn is harvest, and Gi Earth is the field being harvested. Your birth season belonged to Metal, and Earth gives birth to Metal, so your chart spends itself on output: care, competence, keeping everyone fed. In the relationship you probably handled much of the emotional logistics. Who's upset, who needs what, what's for dinner. When it ended, the work stopped, and that silence is loud. Some of the pull back is genuinely missing them. Some is missing being useful. Those need different answers. The first heals with time. The second heals when you let someone take care of you without earning it first. Start with a friend who'll cook for you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Missing them and missing being needed are not the same feeling.

winter.intro: Winter soil is cold, wet and resting. Your season belonged to Water, Gi, and Earth controls Water, so you carry a lot of feeling and work hard to keep it shaped and useful. In love you probably absorbed tension until the ground went muddy. You may have smoothed things over for so long that the breakup surprised everyone, including you. Winter Gi tends to process slowly, in private, and then suddenly understand everything one ordinary Tuesday. Give that Tuesday room. Don't rush to a conclusion, and don't let checking their profile become a way to manage feelings you'd rather not feel. Warmth is your friend here: sunlight, someone who makes you laugh out loud.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You'll understand it all one ordinary day. No need to force it.

earth.intro: The Earth days are your home weather, Gi. You were born when the season hands over to soil, so your own element runs deep in you. In the relationship you were the garden: you fed, you tended, you made things grow, including them. After the breakup, the pull back is caretaking. You still wonder if they're eating properly, if they're okay, if they've worked it out. Your care is real, but it doesn't have to have their name on it. Plant something you'll get to see bloom yourself.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You can stop watering their garden, Gi. Yours has been waiting.

cliff.text: After a breakup you worry. About them, about what you did wrong, about practical things like who keeps the plant.

sample.text: The thing that pulls you back is the investment.

base.why-it-ended: Gyeong Metal is the blade: direct, loyal, decisive. You say what you mean and expect the same in return. In your last relationship that honesty was a gift, and sometimes a weapon. Under stress you can end a conversation with one sentence that's true and still lands far too hard. Or you decided early what was right and stopped negotiating. Metal souls also tend to end things cleanly once trust breaks. If this ended fast, a line was probably crossed, or you felt one coming. Either way, be honest with yourself about whether you left room for the softer conversation.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You were honest and loyal, Gyeong. Those are rare.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: And sometimes you used honesty like a sword. At dinner.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Grief can show up weeks later. That's normal.

spring.intro: A spring axe has a whole forest in front of it. Your birth season belonged to Wood, Gyeong, and Metal cuts Wood, so you were born facing a lot to handle, with the strength to handle it. In love you probably took charge: decided, fixed, protected. You show care by acting. The breakup might feel like a job left half-done, and that irritates you more than you let on. You may be planning conversations, rehearsing the clean version of the ending. The spring blind spot is effort spread thin, swinging at too many trees at once. Pick one task: your own sleep, your own week. You can't chop your way back into someone's heart, and you shouldn't have to.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rehearsing the perfect closing speech in the shower again? Thought so.

summer.intro: Metal born in summer goes through the forge. Your birth season belonged to Fire, Gyeong, and Fire melts Metal, so you grew up under heat and pressure and came out tempered. You're tough, loyal and allergic to drama. In the relationship you probably took a lot before reacting, then reacted all at once. Clean cut. Done. But summer metal stays warm long after it leaves the fire. You might act finished while still running hot underneath, and that's where the checking comes from. Your pride says don't look back. Your heart keeps looking. Neither is wrong. Let the cooling happen slowly instead of plunging it into cold water and pretending it never glowed.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Still warm after the forge is normal. It means it mattered to you.

autumn.intro: Born in autumn, Gyeong, you're metal at full strength. Metal ruled the season and doubled your element, so you're decisive, principled and very hard to bend. In breakups that usually means one of two things: you ended it sharply, or you refused to let it end until you'd won the point. Either way, the blade was out. Strong autumn metal can confuse being right with being close. You may have been right about plenty. The question worth asking is what being right cost. If you keep checking on them, it might be to confirm your verdict rather than because you miss them. Put the sword down for a week. See what you feel without it in your hand.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You were right. Congratulations. Was being right warm at night?

winter.intro: Winter Gyeong is cold steel beside a dark river. Water was in command when you were born, and Metal generates Water, so your toughness flows out as thought, strategy and quiet feeling. You look composed. Inside, you're running analysis on every exchange from the last three months. In love you probably showed care through loyalty and action, and kept the softer feelings in reserve. After the breakup that reserve is leaking out as late-night thinking. It's not weakness. It's metal finally letting water through. The pull back is often the conversation you never had, the one where you said the soft thing. You can still say it, to a journal, a friend, yourself. It doesn't have to be to them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Write the soft thing down, Gyeong. It deserves to exist somewhere.

earth.intro: You were born in the Earth days, Gyeong, when soil takes over the end of a season. Earth feeds Metal, so you arrived well supplied: steady, sure, hard to shake. In love that made you protective and dependable. It also made you slow to say anything soft. After the breakup, the pull back is pride wrapped as fairness. You want the ending to have been reasonable, and you replay who was right. Ore that stays buried never gets used. Dig out one honest feeling and say it to someone you trust.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Winning the argument about the breakup doesn't fix the breakup, Gyeong.

cliff.text: Your breakups are clean cuts. Once Gyeong Metal decides, it's decided, and you don't do the on-and-off thing.

sample.text: The hook, for you, is usually loyalty, or a question of fairness.

base.why-it-ended: Sin Metal is the jewel: refined, precise, beautiful under pressure. You have taste and standards, and you notice when something is off by a millimeter. In your last relationship you may have felt quietly disappointed for a long time, holding back criticism and polishing things alone. Or one careless word cut deeper than they ever knew. Jewels are hard, and they still scratch. If the ending involved hurt pride, or a sense that they never really saw your worth, that's the core of it. Look at how much you kept inside just to stay graceful.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Your standards aren't too high, Sin. They're just yours.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Then why keep them secret for the whole relationship?

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Choosing wrong once doesn't mean your taste is broken.

spring.intro: A jewel in spring sits in a garden full of things to admire. Wood held the season you were born in, Sin, and Metal shapes Wood, so you were born with a sharp eye and an appetite for beautiful options. In love you have taste. You knew exactly what you wanted the relationship to look like, and you noticed every way it didn't. After the breakup you may be weighing it like a purchase: was it worth it, did you settle, should you go back to it? That framing will keep you circling. Spring Sin does best when the question shifts from was this good enough to was I myself in it. Shine is easier when you're not polishing for someone else.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're reviewing your ex like a handbag return. Two stars, would not rebuy?

summer.intro: A jewel born in summer knows heat. Fire was in command when you were born, Sin, and Fire tests Metal, so you grew up under pressure to stay polished while things got hot. You're sensitive, proud and graceful in a crisis, at least in public. In the relationship, criticism probably cut deeper than they realized. You may have absorbed small comments for months. The breakup can feel like a final verdict on your worth, which is why checking is so tempting: you want to know whether they regret it. Summer jewels are formed by heat, not ruined by it. The pressure made you clearer. Their opinion of you was one light source. It was never the whole room.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Their opinion was one lamp, Sin. You still sparkle in every other light.

autumn.intro: Autumn is jewel season, Sin. Metal ruled your birth month and doubled your own element, so your standards, pride and sense of self are strong and well defined. In love that makes you discerning and hard to fool. It also makes you hard to reach. You might have kept part of yourself behind glass the whole relationship, and the other person sensed it. After the breakup the glass case is locked tight. You look perfect. You may be checking their profile while telling everyone you're over it. Sin needs to remember that being admired and being known are different things. The next time someone gets close, let them see a scratch. It's still a jewel.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Over it, you say. While viewing their story at 1:47am. Sure, Sin.

winter.intro: A jewel in winter water glitters under ice. Water was in command when you were born, Sin, and Metal generates Water, so your sparkle flows out as emotion, insight and very good one-liners. You probably understood the relationship better than you let on, and noticed its cracks early. After the breakup you're likely clear-eyed and still sad, which is a strange pairing. Winter Sin can over-wash a memory: rinsing it until it's flawless, or rinsing it until it's ruined. Neither version is the real one. The pull back usually comes from the flawless version. Write down both, the good and the hard, in plain words. A clean stone is an honest stone, not a perfect one.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Write the good and the hard side by side. Both were true.

earth.intro: Late in each season come the Earth days, and you were born inside them, Sin. Earth feeds Metal, so a jewel sits in rich soil: supported, but at risk of being covered over. In the relationship you may have dimmed yourself to keep things smooth, polishing their life while yours collected dust. After it ended, the pull back is the version of you they saw, the one who was chosen. You are still that person. Wash the soil off. One small thing that makes you feel precise and polished again, done for nobody but you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You didn't lose your shine, Sin. It just got buried for a bit.

cliff.text: You break up beautifully. Sin Metal stays composed, says the right things, looks wonderful the following week.

sample.text: The hook, for you, is often the idea of them.

base.why-it-ended: Im Water is the ocean: vast, free, always moving. You bring adventure and big ideas into a relationship, and you need room to roam. Your partner may have loved your freedom and then felt they couldn't hold on to any of it. Or you felt the walls closing in, the routines and expectations, and quietly drifted a little further out each week. Ocean souls rarely slam doors. They let the tide go out. If this ended in distance rather than drama, look at when you started swimming away emotionally, and whether you ever told them why.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You brought adventure into their life, Im. That mattered.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: You also left emotionally three months before you left for real.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Missing them from far away is a very ocean feeling.

spring.intro: Spring Im Water is the river in flood season, pouring into everything that grows. Wood held the season you were born in and Water feeds Wood, so your energy flows outward as ideas, encouragement and adventure. In the relationship you probably helped them grow: new plans, new places, bigger dreams. After the breakup the flow has nowhere to go, and you may feel restless rather than sad. Lots of plans, lots of movement, quick distractions. Spring Water can drain itself feeding others and only notice once the riverbed shows. If you keep checking on them, it might be to see what grew from all that water. Some of it did. Now pour some into your own field.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You helped them grow so much. Now water your own garden, Im.

summer.intro: An ocean in summer runs warm and busy. Fire was in command when you were born, Im, and Water controls Fire, so you were born managing a lot of heat: other people's excitement, demands, big plans. In love you likely kept things moving, cooled fights down, steered toward fun. The breakup might have come after a long stretch of you handling everything and feeling nothing. Summer Water evaporates fastest. You may feel drained and oddly detached, then get hit by a wave three weeks later. That's normal for you. The checking is often the wave looking for a shore. Don't fight the tide. Let it come in, let it go out, and rest somewhere cool in between.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Felt nothing for three weeks, then sobbed at a cereal ad. Classic summer Im.

autumn.intro: Autumn Im Water flows out of mountain stone, cold and clear. Your season belonged to Metal, and Metal generates Water, so your chart is well supported: deep, confident, hard to contain. In love you bring range and freedom. You also bring a current that's hard to hold. The person you lost may have loved the depth and struggled with the tide. After the breakup you probably moved on fast on the surface, new places and new people, while the deep water kept circling the old story. Strong autumn Water's blind spot is assuming you can always leave and always return. People aren't harbors that wait. Spend a little time still, and see what's actually down there.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You can't drift off and expect the harbor to keep your spot.

winter.intro: Born in winter, Im, you're the ocean at its fullest. You were born while Water was in charge and doubled your element, so your feelings run vast, deep and mostly invisible. In love you probably went all in quietly, with a lot happening under a calm surface. When it ended, you might have frozen over: functional, social, unreadable. The risk for winter Water is drowning in your own depth. You can think about a person for a very long time without saying a word. If the checking has become a ritual, that's the cold current talking. Structure helps you: routines, firm plans, a friend who asks direct questions. Give the ocean a shoreline.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: So much happens under your surface, Im. Let one friend see it.

earth.intro: Im, your birthday sits in the Earth days, when a season ends and the ground takes command. Earth controls Water, so the ocean met its banks early: rules, limits, people who expected you to stay in your lane. In love you may have felt contained, or you may have been the one testing every wall. After the breakup the pull back is the shape they gave you. Without banks, water spreads thin. Build your own shoreline: a weekly plan, a friend who checks in, a routine that holds you without holding you back.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Missing the walls isn't missing them, Im. Build your own.

cliff.text: Your pattern is moving on by moving. New plans, new places, new people, maybe a trip booked within a week.

sample.text: You keep circling back because of curiosity and nostalgia.

base.why-it-ended: Gye Water is the rain, the mist, the quiet water that gets into everything. You're intuitive and gentle, and you feel the mood of a room before anyone speaks. In your last relationship you probably sensed every shift and adjusted yourself to soothe it. Rain doesn't always announce itself. You may have kept your real feelings vague, hoping they'd guess. Partners often love the mystery at first and then struggle with never quite knowing where they stand. Look at the gap between what you felt and what you actually said. That gap is where most of this story lives.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You felt everything they felt, Gye. That's a rare gift.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Then you hoped they'd guess your feelings. They didn't. They never do.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Your inner world is comforting. Visit, don't move in.

spring.intro: Spring rain, Gye, is the gentle kind that makes everything grow. You were born while Wood was in charge and Water feeds Wood, so your care flows out softly: noticing, listening, quietly helping someone bloom. In the relationship you probably gave more emotional support than anyone saw. The breakup may have left you feeling invisible, like the rain nobody thanks for the flowers. That's where the checking comes from. You want to see whether what you poured in still shows. It does, in them and in you. Spring Gye needs to remember that rain can fall on its own garden too. Turn the attention you gave them inward for a while.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Nobody thanks the rain, Gye. I'm thanking you. Now rain on yourself.

summer.intro: A summer shower vanishes on hot pavement. You were born while Fire was in charge, Gye, and Water controls Fire, so you were born handling a lot of heat. In love you probably tried to cool things down, soothe their temper, keep the peace. It's exhausting work for a small cloud. After the breakup you may feel wrung out and unusually foggy. Summer Gye sometimes stays attached because the relationship was the most intense weather you'd felt, and calm skies seem empty by comparison. Calm is not empty. It's recovery. Let your reserves refill with Metal: structure, clear routines, people who are reliable rather than thrilling.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Calm feels boring because you got used to storms. Boring is healing, babe.

autumn.intro: Autumn mist rises off cold stone, Gye. Metal was in command when you were born and Metal generates Water, so your intuition is well fed and unusually sharp. You probably saw the end coming before anyone said it, maybe before they knew it themselves. That clarity doesn't make it hurt less. It makes it hurt earlier and longer. After the breakup you might be replaying signs you noticed and ignored. Be gentle about that. Seeing something and being ready to act on it are two separate skills. Autumn Gye's blind spot is living in the knowing instead of the doing. The pull back is your intuition still talking. Thank it, then give it a new subject.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You saw it coming months ago. Knowing early isn't the same as failing.

winter.intro: Winter Gye is snow, Water at its quietest and fullest. The season doubled your element, so you feel deeply, imagine vividly and keep most of it to yourself. In love you probably built an entire inner world around the person, rich and private. After the breakup, that world is still standing, fully furnished, and you visit it at night. That's the pull. It isn't really about whether they'd return. It's that the imagined version is so detailed it feels like somewhere you live. Winter Water needs warmth and earth: sunlight, a body moving, something solid in your hands. Snow melts into spring. You won't stay frozen in this.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: That inner world is beautiful, Gye. Visit by day, not every night.

earth.intro: Born in the Earth days, Gye, you are rain landing on dry ground at the end of a season. Earth controls Water, so a lot of what you gave sank in and disappeared from view. In love you noticed everything and said a fraction of it, while the relationship quietly absorbed you. After the breakup, the pull back is the muddy middle: not over, not reopened, just unclear. You don't have to solve it to move. Give your feelings a container they can't soak away into: a journal, a voice memo, a long walk with one friend.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your feelings didn't vanish, Gye. They soaked in. Let some out.

cliff.text: You grieve softly and privately. Gye Water absorbs feelings, yours and theirs, so you may be carrying their sadness along with your own.

sample.text: You keep circling back because of the emotional bond, the sense that you understood each other without words.
